clue.text: Receiving bill, go white in appearance

indicators.note: the colour-losing verb takes in the bill, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: to go white is to lose colour, to fade
AC is short for account, a bill to be paid

explanation.surface: Someone handed an unwelcome bill turns pale in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiving' is the container signal. 'Go white' suggests fear, but here it simply means to lose colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is a false front or outward show, the face a thing presents to the world.

parts.note: Americans call autumn the fall
back means having come back, returned

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws when autumn comes round again in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallback is a position to withdraw to, a reserve option when plans fail.

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate or subdue
lip is cheek or insolent talk

explanation.surface: A gardener's flower puts down cheeky backchat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primrose' is a family name here: the cowslip is a yellow-flowered plant of the primrose family.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a wild flower of the primula genus, closely related to the common primrose.

indicators.note: the pleasure-seekers come to grief and fall apart, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Pleasure-seekers without morals end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come to grief' rearranges HEDONISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without scruples is untrustworthy and lacking honesty.

clue.text: False incentive to take promissory notes

parts.note: a spur is a goad or stimulus to act
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A dodgy inducement involving signed promises to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious means fake or not genuine, the sense of an untrue claim.

clue.text: Proof I work with Windows — so simple to control

definitions.meaning: a glazier's evidence of the job: the window sealant in their grip
easily manipulated, wholly under one's influence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' looks like computer software, but it means glass panes: a glazier fixing them has the sealing paste in their hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone easily manipulated is compared to soft glazier's paste, moulded at will.

clue.text: Governor helps one to go straight

definitions.meaning: one who governs, such as a monarch
a measuring strip used to draw straight lines

explanation.definitionFit: A monarch or governor holds sway, and a straightedge guides a pencil along a straight line.

clue.text: Where to grow fruit or vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy green vegetable related to beet

explanation.surface: Choosing what to plant: fruit trees or greens.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plantation of fruit trees.

indicators.note: the melons sprawl untamed, so their letters run into a wild new order

explanation.surface: A summer month when the melon patch runs riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month but is the adjective meaning dignified. 'Grow wild' rearranges MELONS.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means grand and dignified, inspiring grave respect.

clue.text: Spirited march goes on, though this is gravely decaying

definitions.text: Spirited march goes on, though this is gravely decaying

parts.words: Spirited march goes on, though this is gravely decaying
parts.note: an American Civil War song about an abolitionist whose corpse moulders in the grave while his soul marches on

explanation.surface: A lively tune keeps going even as its subject rots in the grave.
explanation.walkthrough: The song says the hero 'lies a-mouldering in the grave' but 'his soul goes marching on'; 'spirited' is his soul, and 'gravely' means in the grave.
explanation.definitionFit: This rousing marching song tells of a body mouldering in the grave while its soul marches on.

parts.note: the deepest point is the lowest one
oft is an old word for often, happening regularly

explanation.surface: A claim that some harbour has the deepest water, made again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letters signal, but it is a synonym for OFT. LOWESTOFT is a fishing port on the Suffolk coast of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowestoft is a harbour town in Suffolk, England's most easterly port.

definitions.meaning: close at hand, in the neighbourhood

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a count here but 'one that numbs', read as NUMB-ER; a dentist's injection is a local.
explanation.definitionFit: A local anaesthetic deadens feeling in one place, and something in the neighbourhood is close by.

definitions.meaning: a round-bowled snifter for brandy is named after an inflatable
an inflatable toy found at a child's birthday celebration

explanation.definitionFit: A balloon glass is a wide-bowled snifter, and inflated rubber toys decorate birthday celebrations.

clue.text: Distance a marine goes to give support at sea

parts.note: a yard is a measure of length or distance
RM stands for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: How far a soldier of the sea travels to help a ship in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support at sea' is the definition: a yardarm is the end of the spar that carries a square sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is an outer part of the horizontal spar holding a sail on a ship's mast.

clue.text: Police led to drug in wood

parts.note: cops is an informal name for the police
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Officers lead a narcotics trail into the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket or group of trees.

clue.text: Agree end will be horrible for traitor

indicators.note: the two words are made into a horrible mess, a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Agreeing on an ending will turn out badly for the turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will be horrible' rearranges AGREE and END into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause or party, a turncoat or apostate.

indicators.note: organising these words means arranging their letters into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A colonel is told to build up the structure of his unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' rearranges A REGIMENT; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To germinate is to sprout and start growing, as a seed does.

indicators.note: say tells the solver to go by how a word sounds when spoken

parts.note: pecked means kissed lightly
oral means done by mouth

explanation.surface: A kiss given with the lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the homophone: a past-tense verb ending -ED is often heard as -T. 'Kissed' as a light peck makes the surface misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: A pectoral is one of the large chest muscles.

clue.text: No actors available for Robinson Crusoe?

definitions.meaning: if the cast is away, no performers can be found
Defoe's hero, shipwrecked alone on an island

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the answer as two words: the cast is away.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwrecked sailor left on an island is the type of Defoe's marooned hero, and an absent cast leaves no performers.

indicators.note: processed food is reworked, so the letters of the delicacy are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Appetite for fish roe that has been prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Processed' rearranges CAVIARE. The ellipsis links this clue to the next, which also opens with 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is a craving for wealth, an excessive desire to acquire.

clue.text: Disruptive trumpeter who's left the band?

definitions.meaning: an elephant, which trumpets, living apart from its herd

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpeter' suggests a musician and 'band' a group of players, but the trumpeter is an elephant and the band its herd: a rogue elephant lives alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wayward and uncontrollable is rogue, as is a savage elephant driven from the herd.

parts.note: an eater consumes food

explanation.surface: Continuing the caviare: the larger helping goes to the hungry Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater means larger in size, the comparative of great.

definitions.meaning: British slang for nerve or guts
a heavy drinker is said to hit the ...

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'bottle' means nerve, as in losing one's bottle; to hit the bottle is to drink heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is slang bottle in Britain, and a container of liquor is what a heavy drinker hits.

clue.text: No mountainous regions produce these fruits

parts.note: no means nothing, which is the letter O
ranges are lines of mountains

explanation.surface: Highland country cannot grow these citrus crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are citrus fruits grown in warm climates.

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A frustrated cry that there is no fun to be had.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty relish or zest in doing something.

indicators.note: the insect takes the fruit within itself, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an ant is a small social insect
a lime is a green citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Something for a bug to eat, with fruit on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Including' is the container signal; 'for' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment or sustenance.

definitions.meaning: a pair of matching single beds in one room
siblings born together, who may be brothers

explanation.definitionFit: Twin beds are a matched pair of singles, and siblings born at one birth may be brothers.

clue.text: Valuable picture almost red after restoration

indicators.note: restoring a painting reworks it, so these two words are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A precious painting comes back from the restorer looking nearly crimson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After restoration' signals the anagram; 'almost' looks like a signal to drop a letter, but its letters all go into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a painting by a great European artist before about 1800, usually worth a fortune.

clue.text: Organs joined in harmony, as one sees

parts.note: an eye is an organ of sight
to, as in 'pushed to', means shut or joined
the plural gives a second organ of sight

explanation.surface: Two body parts linked up, agreeing on how things look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organs' gives both eyes, and 'joined' is TO between them. To see eye to eye is to agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of one mind, in agreement, is the idiom of seeing things the same way.

definitions.note: the 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place holds the other piece within it
making the tree new means rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Some bird's habitat has a freshly planted tree in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the tree into ETRE, and 'includes' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A petrel is a seabird that flies low over the ocean waves.
